hints.title: Frequency Containment Property
hints.text: Every substring covering character frequencies of word2 is valid. For any valid window word1[left..right], all right endpoints through n - 1 are also valid.

hints.title: Two-Pointer Sliding Window
hints.text: Maintain frequency counts of the current window and track how many distinct characters meet their target frequency.

hints.title: Suffix Extension Summation
hints.text: When satisfied equals the number of distinct characters in word2, add n - right to the total and shrink left until the window becomes invalid.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def validSubstringCount(self, word1: str, word2: str) -> int:
        from collections import Counter
        target = Counter(word2)
        needed = len(target)
        
        window = Counter()
        satisfied = 0
        left = 0
        ans = 0
        n = len(word1)
        
        for right in range(n):
            ch = word1[right]
            window[ch] += 1
            if ch in target and window[ch] == target[ch]:
                satisfied += 1
                
            while satisfied == needed:
                # Every substring ending from right to n - 1 is valid
                ans += n - right
                l_ch = word1[left]
                if l_ch in target and window[l_ch] == target[l_ch]:
                    satisfied -= 1
                window[l_ch] -= 1
                left += 1
                
        return ans
```

complexity.notes: Both pointers move monotonically from 0 to n in O(n) total operations.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: O(n^2) substring inspection is impossible for n up to 10^5.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Linear sliding window solution scaling cleanly to 10^5.
